newsitem.title: USA: Hercules forms venture with Danish company.
newsitem.headline: Hercules forms venture with Danish company.

text.p: Hercules Inc on Thursday said it formed a joint venture with Denmark's Jacob Holm & Sons AS that will produce thermal-bond fibers for the non-wovens industry.

Hercules said in a statement the venture would involve a as combination of its fibers division with Jacob Holm's Danaklon Group. It said it would own 51 percent of the venture, which will make fine denier polypropylene staple fiber.
A Hercules spokesman declined to comment on financial terms of the transaction.
The venture, with head offices in Wilmington, Delaware, will make the fiber for the hygiene, industrial, automotive and decorative fabric markets.
Hercules said its division made staple fiber used in non-woven fabrics for disposable diapers and other hygienic products.
Jacob Holm is a holding company whose operational center, Danaklon, makes specialized polypropylene and bicomponent fibers for the hygiene industry.
Hercules said the combined businesses had sales of about $300 million in 1996.
